newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro -bank takes share in its Polish unit.
newsitem.headline: Metro -bank takes share in its Polish unit.

text.p: German retail group Metro AG said on Wednesday it would sell 25 percent of its operations in Poland to a Warsaw bank as part of a broad expansion program in the country.

Bank Handlowy Warsaw SA would buy the stake as a first step toward issuing shares in the Polish unit in the next three to five years, Metro said in a statement released in Germany after a news conference in Warsaw.

Metro's is already represented in Poland through its Vobis Microcomputer Sp., Tip Discount Polska Sp., Praktiker Polska and Real Sp. chains. The joint venture in which Bank Handlowy was taking a share would include Real and Tip Discount.
The commercial bank would also support Metro's plans to open more than two dozen new stores and five large shopping malls in Poland in the next two years, Metro said.
The malls would include outlets of Metro stores specialising in clothing, computer, electronics and other wares as well as 60 to 80 locally owned shops, services and restaurants.

The first was due to open in Czeladz at the end of this year. Four more housing a total of 17 Metro stores would follow in 1998. Another 12 Metro stores were planned for other locations, the company said.
Metro expected to employ 10,000 Poles by the end of 1998.
"The future development of Metro decidedly depends on the internationalisation of our operations," Metro chief executive Klaus Wiegandt said. "Poland has absolute strategic priority."
Metro also said it would donate one million zloty to the Polish Red Cross for victims of the catastrophic flooding along the Oder and Niesse rivers.

Earlier this month Metro said it expected 1997 operating profit to exceed last year's total of 1.062 billion marks, and forecast a loss of 100 million marks from international start-up operations in Poland, Turkey and China.
It said 1997 sales should rise almost five percent to about 65 billion marks, not including about 950 million marks from Vobis' takeover of PC assembler Peacock AG.
